newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended near Thusrday's closing levels in what dealers said was a non-event day.

Some bargain hunting in afternoon trade helped reverse some losses in gold and industrial shares but the market struggled to find direction with Wall Street closed on Thursday night for the Thanksgiving holiday.
"We opened weak but now we have turned around...Sentiment is not there. It has been a non-event today," a dealer said.
Dealers said some futures activity in early trade hurt shares in the morning but the market held up well faced with a weaker rand and long bonds.
Volumes picked up slightly in afternoon trade but were generally moderate on the day, they said.
They said players continued to be wary of gold shares as the bullion price looked sickly.
"There is some bargain hunting in golds but we are not going to see them better. Maybe some guys think this is bottom but a lot of people are scared of them," one said.

The market was seen better next week as the futures close-out in mid-December approached. They said players could also return to the market after shying away on an erratic electronic trading system which interrupted trade this week.
The overall index ended off 0.2 points to 6,713.9, the industrial index lost 2.9 points to 7,997.5 and the gold index was down 3.0 points to 1,523.7 points.
Anglo added 400 cents to 262.50 rand, De Beers rose 175 cents to 140.75 rand, Richemont gained 50 cents to 68.75 rand and Sasol slipped 50 cents to 57 rand.
Western Areas climbed 150 cents to 64.50 rand, Freegold dropped 55 cents to 34 rand and Kloof was up five cents to 37.80 rand.

Near-term industrial and all-share futures ended firmer in quiet trade and dealers said the premium to spot indicated that players wanted to push the market higher as the futures close-out approached.
Golds were static to slightly weaker but were seen easier next week on a struggling bullion price.
The December all-share contract was at 6,160/93 from 6,145 settlement on Thursday, the gold contract was at 1,066/80 from 1,078 and industrials at 7,750/55 from 7,741.
